source.title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Hao-Ran Jin; Xi-Ting Wang; Shijie Ren; Hong Xie; De-Fu Lian

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices and tables, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly measures SAE feature splitting, absorption, and directional overlap in LLM activations. Its results qualify the view that SAE features are complete canonical units: standard SAEs show these pathologies, and the proposed regularizer reduces but does not eliminate them.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own measurements of SAE feature splitting, absorption, and decoder-direction overlap; these are included. Cited findings from other work are excluded. Reconstruction, interpretability, and downstream task results are not cataloged because they do not directly measure the claim versions being tested. Main-figure values without numerical descriptions are not entered as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper proposing the C2R regularizer, but it reports its own SAEBench measurements of absorption and splitting for standard SAEs (Batch TopK, TopK, AbsTopK, Ort) on Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3-8B and Qwen3-8B. It also shows dictionary structure shifting with the training objective on the same activations. Both bear on whether SAE latents are complete, canonical units (V5). Comparisons of C2R with other methods, its ablations and its lambda sweep are the method's own performance and do not bear on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that C2R mitigates splitting and absorption, lowers composition, and preserves reconstruction, interpretability and disentanglement. The guarantee is conditional, holding in 88.1% of absorption pairs, and C2R may suppress legitimate polysemanticity. Splitting is not eliminated, and on Qwen3-8B it is unchanged across all methods.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops and evaluates a batchwise SAE regularizer using activation norms and decoder cosine gating; it does not reproduce the toy-network feature-superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Structural metrics vary with C2R regularization strength, SAE backbone, layer, model, and training data. At lambda_C2R = 10, structural scores improve further but reconstruction fidelity begins to degrade.

fits_no_version.finding: Decoder-direction redundancy (mean max cosine similarity) is about 0.27–0.34 for Batch TopK and TopK SAEs. It falls to about 0.07–0.10 under C2R or OrtSAE on the same model activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Redundancy and overlap among SAE latent directions is largely set by the training objective rather than by the model's representation.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The main experiments center on one model and layer, with some extensions to two 8B models and other conditions. Feature structure is assessed through proxy metrics rather than ground-truth feature identities. The paper states the theoretical guarantee is conditional; its AutoInterp assessment uses a proprietary judge, though it reports human and alternate-judge checks. Some main results are shown only in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 9–13 values for comparator methods other than Batch TopK, and Table 14–16 results outside the listed structural metrics, are omitted to keep the row set focused on the principal SAE-unit measures. Figure 3 structural comparisons are described qualitatively but lack extractable exact values in the text.

untested.parts: No toy models; no test of sparsity-dependent transitions or geometry.
No test of capacity competition as the cause of neuron polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.
SAEs are assumed to recover features; neuron-level distribution and ground-truth recovery are not tested.
Feature-by-feature stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, and completeness beyond the absorption and splitting probes, are not tested. The 5 seeds report only aggregate metrics.

missing.what: Absorption and splitting for all baselines across sparsity k=60–120 (figure only, no numbers in text)
Per-letter absorption rates for a Batch TopK SAE, ranging up to about 0.6 for some letters, and their correlation with frequency (Pearson r=0.301, p=0.135)
Count of absorption pairs found in trained 65k-latent SAEs (N=4,555–4,947)
TopK baseline absorption and split values in Tables 11–12, which show larger pathologies than Batch TopK

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a mitigation-method paper. Its bearing on V5 comes only from the baseline SAE measurements and from the dependence of dictionary structure on the objective. The reader's labels conflated C2R improvement with V5 states. The ablation and lambda-sweep rows (r19–r34) are own-method rows and are not linked.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse-feature superposition, and its sparsity-dependent geometric transition are not tested.
The paper discusses SAE dictionary capacity but does not test whether neuron polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
It does not test causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.
It does not directly test whether features in LLMs are distributed across neurons or whether SAE features recover ground-truth model features.
It measures splitting, absorption, and decoder-vector composition, but does not establish completeness, canonical identity, or feature-by-feature stability across seeds or training choices.
It does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional feature representations.

relationships.condition: Standard SAEs (Batch TopK, TopK, AbsTopK, OrtSAE) on Gemma-2-2B layers 12 and 20, OWT and Pile data, and on Llama-3-8B layer 20
relationships.reason: Measured absorption is 0.06–0.30 and split counts reach 1.15–1.35 (r2, r8, r11, r12, r14, r17, r36, r37, r39, r42, r43). Swapping only the training objective changes these on the same activations, so latents are not canonical units.
relationships.display_finding: Measured absorption was 0.06–0.30 and split counts reached 1.15–1.35, and swapping only the training objective on the same activations changed these values, so latents were not canonical units.

relationships.condition: Mild splitting conditions (Gemma layer 12 Batch TopK/Ort, Llama Batch TopK, Gemma OWT and Pile) and Qwen3-8B layer 20
relationships.reason: Split counts are only 1.04–1.19 (r3, r9, r15, r18, r40). On Qwen3-8B, absorption is below 0.01 for all SAEs (r5) and split is a constant 1.1154 (r6), so the size of the pathology depends on the model.
relationships.display_finding: Split values were only 1.04–1.19; on Qwen3-8B absorption stayed below 0.01 for all SAEs and split was a constant 1.1154, so the size of the pathology depended on the model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Vanilla Batch TopK SAE results on Gemma-2-2B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama-3-8B settings reported in Tables 8–13
reader_labels.reason: The reported nonzero composition, absorption, and splitting scores show that the tested learned latents are not uniformly non-overlapping, unsplit canonical units (r1-r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: C2R-enhanced SAEs across tested models, layers, datasets, regularization strengths, and SAE backbones
reader_labels.reason: C2R generally reduces these pathologies, but residual nonzero scores remain; stronger regularization also begins to degrade reconstruction fidelity (r1-r18, r25-r43).
